description:
This record is the image-bearing manifestation of Lee Sharks’s poem *if your heart should ever slowly turn*. Its deposited body contains a single externally hosted PNG reference rather than extracted verse. The absence of body text is therefore not evidence of an empty or failed deposit: the image is the primary artifact in this manifestation.

The poem’s complete textual manifestation appears separately as record #734. The two records should be related as parallel expressions of one work rather than collapsed as duplicates. #733 preserves the visual presentation; #734 supplies searchable, accessible, and citation-ready text. Because the frozen repository body exposes only the image URL, no description should invent typography, color, composition, or other visual particulars not visible in the source text. The authority record should identify the image as complete in its own medium while using the companion record to restore accessibility and retrieval.

wiki_article:
**if your heart should ever slowly turn** is a short lyric poem by Lee Sharks preserved in both visual and textual forms.

Record #733 is the visual manifestation. Its repository body points to a PNG hosted through Blogger, making the image—not a transcription—the primary file represented by the deposit. Record #734 preserves the poem as plain text.

The dual deposit allows the work to retain its visual presentation while also remaining searchable and accessible. The records are related manifestations of the same poem, not redundant copies. The image record should therefore remain active even when the text is available elsewhere.

The repository does not expose enough information to describe the image’s visual design reliably. Any future visual description should be prepared from the deposited image itself and should distinguish observed layout from interpretation.
